newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Treasury gap deficit seen widening.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Treasury gap deficit seen widening.

text.p: A Moroccan think-tank said on Tuesday that it expected the country's Treasury deficit gap to widen in 1997 due to economic stagnation and drop of tax receipts.

An expected drop in tax receipts and liberalisation of banking interest rates will push towards a widening gap of the deficit, the independent Centre Maorocain de Conjoncture (CMC) said but gave no figures.

Commenting on the forecast in a CMC newsletter to be released soon, a CMC analyst said: "The financing of treasury deficit...will face serious problems this year due mainly to the economy's stagnation and tax receipt drop."
According to official provisional figures quoted by the centre, the Treasury deficit rose to 10.2 billion dirhams ($1.09 billion) in 1996, from 9.4 billion dirhams in the previous year.
In recent years receipts declined respectively to 69.6 billion dirhams in 1994, 62.7 billion in 1995 but suddenly rose to 75.07 billion dirhams last year, the centre said.
"But our forecast is that the receipts should drop in 1997 because 1996 was an exceptional year," it added.
To comply with the World Trade Organisation rules, Morocco is dismantling customs barriers, reducing taxes on companies and on exported goods, officials said.

The centre also said that previously the Treasury had benefited from public financing at an interest rate of around 4.25 percent. "But with the continuing financial reforms, the Treasury will be obliged to deal with the financial market's interest rate of up to 12 percent."

The Treasury also benefited from an exceptional 6.0 billion dirhams state financial envelope to finance its deficit in 1995 which coincided with a severe drought and GDP negative growth of minus 7.6 percent, the expert said.

In an earlier newsletter, the centre predicted: "On the basis of the climate...we expect a stagnation of Morocco's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 1997 and probably a negative growth of minus one percent in the worst of cases, due mainly to an expected 50 percent drop in cereals harvest."
Agricultural activity represents nearly 20 percent of Morocco's GDP and employs 50 percent of the country's estimated 10 million workforce.
GDP totalled $34.7 billion in 1996 against $31.8 billion in 1995, the Statistics Directorate said.
